part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: And they went on past Sinope, and many a mighty river?Ts mouth, and past many a barbarous tribe, and the cities of the Amazons, the warlike women of the East, till all night they heard the clank of anvils and the roar of furnace-blasts, and the forge-fires shone like sparks through the darkness in the mountain glens aloft; for they were come to the shores of the Chalybes, the smiths who never tire, but serve Ares the cruel War-god, forging weapons day and night.

translation.en: They sailed past Sinope, numerous mighty river mouths, and many foreign tribes.
translation.kr: 그들은 시노페와 수많은 거대한 강어귀, 그리고 많은 이국적인 부족들을 지나쳐 항해했습니다.

translation.en: They passed the cities of the Amazons, the fierce warrior women of the East.
translation.kr: 그리고 동방의 사나운 여전사들인 아마존족의 도시들을 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: All night they heard the clank of anvils and the roar of furnace blasts.
translation.kr: 밤새도록 모루를 두드리는 소리와 용광로가 뿜어내는 굉음이 들려왔습니다.

translation.en: Forge fires shone like sparks through the darkness in the mountain glens above.
translation.kr: 저 위쪽 산골짜기에서는 대장간의 불빛이 어둠 속에서 불꽃처럼 빛났습니다.

translation.en: They had reached the shores of the Chalybes, the tireless smiths.
translation.kr: 그들은 지칠 줄 모르는 대장장이들인 칼리베스족의 해안에 도착한 것이었습니다.

translation.en: These smiths forged weapons day and night to serve Ares, the cruel god of war.
translation.kr: 이 대장장이들은 잔혹한 전쟁의 신 아레스를 모시며 밤낮으로 무기를 만들었습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: And at day-dawn they looked eastward, and midway between the sea and the sky they saw white snow-peaks hanging, glittering sharp and bright above the clouds.  And they knew that they were come to Caucasus, at the end of all the earth: Caucasus the highest of all mountains, the father of the rivers of the East.  On his peak lies chained the Titan, while a vulture tears his heart; and at his feet are piled dark forests round the magic Colchian land.

translation.en: At dawn they looked eastward and saw white snow peaks hanging between sea and sky.
translation.kr: 동이 트자 그들은 동쪽을 바라보았고, 바다와 하늘 사이에 새하얀 설봉들이 떠 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: The peaks glittered sharply and brightly above the clouds.
translation.kr: 그 봉우리들은 구름 위에서 날카롭고 눈부시게 반짝였습니다.

translation.en: They knew they had reached the Caucasus mountains at the very end of the earth.
translation.kr: 그들은 세상의 끝에 있는 코카서스산맥에 도착했다는 것을 깨달았습니다.

translation.en: The Caucasus was the highest of all mountains and the father of Eastern rivers.
translation.kr: 코카서스는 모든 산 중에서 가장 높았으며 동방으로 흐르는 강들의 아버지였습니다.

translation.en: A Titan lay chained on its peak while a vulture tore at his heart.
translation.kr: 그 산 정상에는 티탄족 하나가 사슬에 묶인 채 독수리에게 심장을 뜯기고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Below its feet, dark forests surrounded the magical land of Colchis.
translation.kr: 그 산기슭 아래로는 마법의 땅 콜키스를 둘러싼 울창하고 어두운 숲이 펼쳐져 있었습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: And they rowed three days to the eastward, while Caucasus rose higher hour by hour, till they saw the dark stream of Phasis rushing headlong to the sea, and, shining above the tree-tops, the golden roofs of King Aietes, the child of the Sun.

translation.en: They rowed eastward for three days as the Caucasus rose higher every hour.
translation.kr: 그들은 사흘 동안 동쪽으로 노를 저었고, 코카서스산맥은 시간마다 더 높이 솟아올랐습니다.

translation.en: Finally, they saw the dark stream of the Phasis river rushing wildly into the sea.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 바다로 거세게 흘러드는 파시스강의 어두운 물줄기를 보았습니다.

translation.en: Above the treetops shone the golden roofs of King Aeetes, child of the Sun.
translation.kr: 그리고 나무 꼭대기 위로는 태양의 아들 아이에테스 왕의 황금빛 지붕들이 빛나고 있었습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then out spoke Ancaios the helmsman, ?~We are come to our goal at last, for there are the roofs of Aietes, and the woods where all poisons grow; but who can tell us where among them is hid the golden fleece?  Many a toil must we bear ere we find it, and bring it home to Greece.?T

translation.en: Then Ancaeus the helmsman spoke up to the crew.
translation.kr: 그때 조타수 안카이오스가 선원들에게 말했습니다.

translation.en: We have finally reached our goal, for there are the roofs of Aeetes.
translation.kr: 우리는 마침내 목적지에 도달했소. 저기에 아이에테스의 지붕들이 보이기 때문이오.

translation.en: There are the woods where all deadly poisons grow.
translation.kr: 모든 치명적인 독초들이 자라는 숲도 저기에 있소.

translation.en: But who can tell us where the Golden Fleece is hidden among them?
translation.kr: 하지만 그 숲 어디에 황금 양모가 숨겨져 있는지 누가 우리에게 말해줄 수 있겠소?

translation.en: We must endure many hardships before we find it and bring it home to Greece.
translation.kr: 그것을 찾아 그리스의 고향으로 가져가기 전까지 우리는 많은 고난을 견뎌내야만 할 것이오.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: But Jason cheered the heroes, for his heart was high and bold; and he said, ?~I will go alone up to Aietes, though he be the child of the Sun, and win him with soft words.  Better so than to go altogether, and to come to blows at once.?T  But the Minuai would not stay behind, so they rowed boldly up the stream.

translation.en: But Jason cheered the heroes, for his heart was courageous and bold.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 용감하고 대담한 마음씨를 지녔기에 영웅들을 격려했습니다.

translation.en: I will go up to Aeetes alone, even though he is the child of the Sun.
translation.kr: 그가 비록 태양의 아들이라 할지라도, 나 홀로 아이에테스에게 올라가겠소.

translation.en: I will try to win him over with gentle words.
translation.kr: 부드러운 말로 그를 설득해 보도록 하겠소.

translation.en: This is better than going all together and starting a fight immediately.
translation.kr: 다 함께 몰려가 단번에 싸움을 벌이는 것보다 이 편이 나을 것이오.

translation.en: But the Minyans refused to stay behind, so they rowed boldly up the stream.
translation.kr: 그러나 미니아이 사람들은 뒤에 남기를 거부했고, 이내 대담하게 강을 거슬러 노를 저어갔습니다.
